public_rationale: METR's July 14, 2025 report found task time horizons doubling roughly every seven months, with possible acceleration to every four months in 2024 [e3]. This does not establish a slowdown relative to 2019–2023 followed by sustained renewed acceleration [e3]. A March 20, 2026 research note also reports increasing sensitivity to analysis choices as the task suite saturates [e4]. These measurements do not settle the eventual-resumption claim [e3, e4].
limitations: No consistent series establishes the required baseline, slowdown and subsequent sustained acceleration.
Task time horizons do not measure all AI progress, and estimates depend on task selection and analysis choices.
The hypothetical five-year slowdown supplies no deadline; a finite slowdown cannot establish that slowdown lasts forever.

conditions: even if the 2019-2023 acceleration slows down for five years, as he has often speculated

statement.excerpt: Even if the AI acceleration we saw from 2019-2023 slows down for five years, as I have often speculated, it won’t slow down forever.
statement.document_title: Hard-forked! Casey Newton’s distorted portrait of Gary Marcus and AI skepticism

from_speaker: the AI acceleration we saw from 2019-2023
our_interpretation: Assess the conditional proposition that a slowdown, if it occurs, eventually ends.
Even if does not assert that a slowdown will occur. Five years describes a hypothetical duration, not a deadline for renewed acceleration.
Renewed acceleration means a sustained increase in the rate of capability progress after an established slowdown, measured on comparable tasks.
The alternative concessive reading makes the eventual-resumption statement broader; it still supplies no deadline.
criteria.support_condition: After a documented slowdown relative to the 2019–2023 pace, comparable longitudinal evidence establishes renewed acceleration.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive event establishes that progress can never accelerate again. A finite period of continued slowdown cannot establish forever.
